name: Shipping chokepoints
value: 2 tankers hit mines east of Hormuz 19–20 Nov
summary: Iran says two tankers hit mines east of Hormuz on 19–20 Nov after a tanker was struck off Khasab on 18 Nov
state: Iran's navy said two tankers that had switched off tracking caught fire after hitting naval mines in a prohibited area east of the Strait of Hormuz on 19–20 Nov, and told ships to coordinate with its forces before transiting (Tasnim; Anadolu). This follows a projectile strike on a tanker off Khasab, Oman, on 18 Nov, with crew safe (Gulf News). Mines and near-daily attacks keep Hormuz traffic materially impeded.
for_you: Expect longer shipping times and higher freight and insurance costs on Gulf routes to feed into fuel and goods prices. Mariners should follow UKMTO and flag-state advisories.
rubric_hit: Hormuz traffic materially impeded by mines and attacks = Alert

sources.title: Tasnim — Tanker catches fire after hitting sea mine in Strait of Hormuz
Anadolu — 2 oil tankers catch fire after hitting mines east of Strait of Hormuz: Iranian army
Gulf News — Tanker disabled, crew safe after strike near Strait of Hormuz

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
